issues.reason: The past-perfect ordering trigger is stated sentence-scoped — "emit the ordering whenever the sentence contains another asserted event for the perfect to precede, whatever links them", with only intra-sentential links exemplified — and "Nightmoths had landed on the lanterns during the night" holds no second event, so omitting Before follows the letter of the rule and emits nothing false; the sentence/text scope clash is the reviewer's own gap 2, a coverage gap rather than a parse defect.

Same standard: "The nightmoths had left silken threads on the lanterns" is likewise a single-event sentence, so the stated trigger does not fire, and a missing ordering atom is an unrecorded inference, not false, ill-typed or over-asserted content.

gaps_confirmed: definite anaphora to a referent that exists only inside a distribution rule — "Mire-essence formed in each cauldron" mints per-member `(sk_essence $x)` terms and nothing lets the next sentence's "the mire-essence" refer to them, so the essence stored is a different entity from the essence formed

the past-perfect ordering test is sentence-scoped ("whenever the sentence contains another asserted event") while its exemption is text-scoped ("no other event in the text"), leaving a perfect alone in its sentence but anchored by a neighbouring sentence of the passage unresolved

"during" + a day-part NP ("during the night"): During is mandated for that surface word but needs two reified eventualities, while day-parts must stay bare Time symbols and may never take a witness, so the two rules cannot both be met
new_gaps: a multi-word proper name denoting a plurality ("the Salt-bloom Tide-pools"): *Names and casing* gives one opaque individual plus a singular type atom and bars `GroupOf` on a named individual, so the referent's plurality (and any count) has no carrier

an entity-attached origin modifier on a bare mass ("sea-water from the Salt-bloom Tide-pools"): an oblique's bare-mass object is told to stay a constant, yet `(From sea_water ...)` on the constant would be a kind-level claim about all sea-water — the faithful reading needs a witness the mass rule does not license
notes: Licensed carriers for the two perfects do exist — `(Before sk_land_1 sk_collect_1)` and `(Before sk_leave_1 sk_collect_1)` — so resolving gap 2 in favour of passage scope would make them mandatory on any later parse. Everything else here follows the instruction set: the group/Cardinality pairs, the each-cauldron rule with its PartOf range, Skolem essence and QuantifierPhrase companion, the "by evening" TimeAtMost, the Source/Goal/Location obliques, and the modifier-genus splits (silken exposed; night, clay, sea, mire not).
